notes: "Recipe from the kitchen of: Vi Sharp."
Two copies of the same pie are in the box. The second, titled "Pumpkin Cream Pie Delight" in a different hand, adds the optional pecans.

recipes.title: Apple Pie (Tapioca)
steps: Combine the tapioca, sugar, salt, spices and apples and let stand 15 minutes.
Put in the crust and dot with butter.
Put on the top crust and bake 55 minutes at 425°.
notes: The "???" beside the nutmeg is the cook's own, the same as on No. 134.

recipes.title: Rhubarb Cream Pie
steps: Blend the sugar, flour, nutmeg and butter and add the eggs.
Pour over the rhubarb in a 9" pie crust. Top with fancy cut pieces of pastry, or a lattice crust.
Bake in a hot oven, 450°, for 10 minutes, then 350° for 30 minutes.
notes: The amounts were later traced over in darker ink.

recipes.title: Double-Flaky Apple Pie
ingredients: Crust: 2 cups sifted flour, 1 teaspoon salt, 3/4 cup Crisco, 1/4 cup water
Filling: 6 large cooking apples, 3/4 cup sugar, 2 tablespoons flour, 1 teaspoon cinnamon, 1 tablespoon butter or margarine
steps: Combine the flour and salt. Cut in the Crisco until the mixture is uniform and fairly coarse. Sprinkle with the water a tablespoon at a time, tossing with a fork. Work into a firm ball.

Divide in two and press into flat circles. On a lightly floured board, roll the bottom crust 1/8 inch thick and 1 1/2 inches larger than the inverted pie plate. Ease into the plate and trim even with the edge.
Pare, core and slice the apples into the crust. Combine the sugar, flour and cinnamon and sprinkle over the apples. Dot with butter.
Moisten the rim with water. Roll the top crust, lift onto the pie, and trim 1/2 inch beyond the edge. Fold the top edge under the bottom crust and flute. Prick the top.
Bake at 400° for 30 to 40 minutes, until the apples are tender and the crust is golden brown.

recipes.title: Pumpkin Pie
steps: Mix in order and pour into an unbaked pie shell.
Bake about 1 hour: 425° for 15 minutes, then 350° for 45 minutes.
notes: The two-temperature baking times were added later in black pen.

recipes.title: Fresh Berry Pie
steps: Combine and put in the crust.
Cover with the top crust and bake about 30 to 45 minutes at 425°.
notes: "to 45" and the 425° were written in later; the original note after them is scribbled out.
flags: The cinnamon amount is written over; 1/4 t is the best reading.
The temperature looks changed from 400° or 450° to 425°.

recipes.title: Pie Crust (Wesson Oil)
steps: Mix the flour and salt.
Add the oil and milk and mix. Press into a ball, divide, roll, and put in the pie tin.
Bake at 425°, or as the filling recipe directs.
notes: Makes a double crust. Oil crusts are easiest to roll between two sheets of waxed paper.

recipes.title: Lemon Cloud Pie
recipes.time: Prep 45 min, ready in 6 hr 45 min
ingredients: 1 Pillsbury refrigerated pie crust (from 15-oz. pkg.), softened as directed
steps: Heat oven to 450°F. Prepare the crust for a one-crust baked shell in a 9-inch glass pie pan. Bake 9 to 11 minutes until light golden brown. Cool completely.

Meanwhile, in a medium saucepan, combine the sugar and cornstarch. Stir in the water, lemon juice and egg yolks. Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until the mixture boils and thickens. Boil 1 minute. Add the cream cheese and lemon peel, stirring until melted and smooth. Cool to room temperature.
In a large bowl, beat the 1/2 cup whipping cream until soft peaks form; fold into the lemon mixture. Spoon into the cooled shell.
Cover the surface with plastic wrap and refrigerate at least 6 hours or overnight. Spoon or pipe the whipped cream topping over the filling. Store in the refrigerator.

recipes.title: "Quick" Lemon Pie
steps: Stir the Cool Whip, lemonade and Eagle Brand milk until smooth.
Pour into the crust.
Refrigerate for 2 hours or overnight.
flags: The lemonade can size is written over; 12 oz. is the best reading.

recipes.title: Rhubarb Pie (Old Fashioned)
steps: Mix the sugar, flour and salt and toss with the rhubarb. Let stand while making the crust.
Put in the crust and dot with butter. Put on the top crust and slit.
Bake at 425° for 40 to 50 minutes, or until browned or bubbling through the slits.
notes: Spelled "Rubarb" on the card.

recipes.title: Impossible Pie
ingredients: 1 cup coconut, plus more for the top
steps: Put everything in the blender and mix until smooth.
Pour into a greased 10" pie pan.
Bake at 350° for 40 to 50 minutes.
Let set 5 minutes and sprinkle with coconut.
notes: Typed with "Dorothy" at the top. It's "impossible" because it makes its own crust as it bakes.
The last step was added by hand.
flags: The flour fraction is faint; 1/2 cup is the usual amount for this pie.

recipes.title: Raisin Cream Pie
steps: Beat the eggs until fluffy and thick.
Add the sugar, spices, salt, lemon juice and butter all at once and blend well.
Fold in the raisins and walnuts and pour into an 8" pastry shell.
Bake at 375° for 30 to 35 minutes. Cool before serving.

recipes.title: Raisin Pie
steps: Combine the filling ingredients.
Bake at 450° till the crust is done.
flags: The card doesn't mention the crust or a time; a double crust and 30 to 40 minutes are typical.
Most raisin pies simmer the raisins, water, sugar and flour until thick before filling the crust.

recipes.title: Apple Betty
ingredients: Topping: 1/4 c butter, 1/2 c brown sugar, 1 c flour, 1/4 tsp salt
steps: Cover the bottom of a pan with thinly sliced apples. Sprinkle with the sugar and cinnamon.
Mix the butter, brown sugar, flour and salt to make coarse crumbs and sprinkle over the apples.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 40 minutes. Serve with cream.
notes: "(8 ounce)" or "8 some" is squeezed in after "apples"; probably about 8 apples.

recipes.title: Apple Bake
recipes.contributor: Duke University Diet and Fitness Cookbook
steps: Slice the apples 1/4 inch thick (leave the peel on) and place in a 9-inch square baking dish sprayed with vegetable spray.
Drain the pineapple, saving the juice. Spread the pineapple over the apples.
Mix the cinnamon, cardamom and sugars and sprinkle over the fruit. Pour the pineapple juice over all and sprinkle with nuts.
Bake 30 minutes at 350°, or until tender. Serve hot or cold.
notes: 85 calories per serving (73 without nuts).

recipes.title: Cinnamon & Sugar Blondies
recipes.format: Handwritten striped card, front and back
ingredients: Cinnamon and sugar to sprinkle over the top
steps: Preheat oven to 350°. Grease an 8" x 11" pan with cooking spray or butter.
Beat the butter and sugars until fluffy. Add the eggs and vanilla and beat until combined.
In a separate bowl, combine the flour, salt, baking soda and cinnamon. Add to the wet ingredients and beat until combined.
Transfer the batter to the pan and sprinkle the top with cinnamon and sugar.
Bake 25 to 30 minutes.
notes: One of Tammy's cards (the striped ones are hers).

recipes.title: Samoa Apples
steps: Slice the apples into 1/4" thick slices. Use a melon baller to remove the cores.
In a bowl, stir the caramel sauce and coconut flakes to combine. Spoon onto the apple slices.
Microwave the chocolate chips and butter, stirring every 30 seconds, until fully melted.
Drizzle over the apples and enjoy.
notes: One of Tammy's cards (the striped ones are hers). Like the Girl Scout cookie, on an apple slice.
flags: The chocolate chips line says just "1/2"; cup assumed.

recipes.title: Caramel Filled Apples
steps: Cut the apples in half and use a melon baller to scoop the centers out.
Pour lemon juice onto the apples so they don't brown so fast.
Heat the caramel squares and corn syrup on low heat. Let cool 10 to 15 minutes.
Pour the caramel into the apples and refrigerate.
When the caramel is solid, slice into bite-size pieces and enjoy.
notes: One of Tammy's cards (the striped ones are hers).
flags: The pecans aren't in the directions; sprinkle them on the caramel before it sets.
The pecan line says just "1/4"; cup assumed.

recipes.title: Apple Crisp (For Anyone or Diabetics)
ingredients: 4 cups apples (not too tart), peeled, cored and sliced
Topping: 1/2 cup flour, 3/4 cup oatmeal, 1/2 teaspoon cinnamon, 2 to 3 tablespoons apple juice concentrate, 2 tablespoons margarine
steps: Combine the first four ingredients in a bowl and arrange in an 8x8 baking dish.
Combine the flour, oatmeal and cinnamon. Cut in the margarine until crumbly.
Drizzle the apple juice concentrate over the crumbs and mix well. Sprinkle over the apple mixture.
Bake at 375° for 30 minutes. Can serve with Cool Whip.
notes: The clipping says "I adjust cinnamon, oatmeal and flour to my taste and want."
Someone typed up a copy; on it the oatmeal was hand-corrected from 1/4 to 3/4 cup to match the clipping.
Diabetic exchanges: 1 fruit, 1 bread, 1/2 fat.
flags: The clipping says 1 teaspoon tapioca; the typed copy says 1 tablespoon.

recipes.title: Baked Rice Pudding
steps: Combine the rice and raisins.
Mix the eggs, sugar and salt.
Add the scalded milk and vanilla and combine everything.
Dot the top with butter and sprinkle with nutmeg.
Bake at 325° for 45 to 55 minutes, until a silver knife comes out clean.

recipes.title: Cranberry Delight
ingredients: 1 can (20 ounces) crushed pineapple, juice drained and reserved
steps: Combine the pineapple juice and water in a 2-qt. saucepan and heat to boiling. Remove from heat, add the gelatin, and stir until dissolved.
Stir in the cranberry sauce, lemon juice, peel and nutmeg. Chill until the mixture thickens slightly.
Add the sour cream and stir until thoroughly combined. Fold in the pineapple and pecans.
Pour into an 8-cup mold and chill until firm. Unmold onto a serving plate and garnish with fresh strawberries if desired.
notes: A molded gelatin salad, the holiday kind.
A handwritten copy is also in the box, titled "Jello salad, Cranberry Delight," from "a magazine," marked "Good, Thanksgiving & Christmas or anytime."

recipes.title: Easy Berry Fruit Tart
recipes.time: Prep 25 min, ready in 2 hr 40 min
ingredients: 1 Pillsbury refrigerated pie crust (from 15-oz. pkg.), softened as directed
steps: Heat oven to 450°F. Prepare the crust for a one-crust baked shell in a 9-inch glass pie pan. Do not prick the crust.

In a food processor, pulse the almonds and sugar until finely ground. Sprinkle over the crust and gently press in. Bake 9 to 11 minutes until light golden brown. If the crust puffs in the center, flatten gently with the back of a wooden spoon. Cool 20 minutes.
Meanwhile, combine the crème fraîche and vanilla pudding and blend well.
Spread the pudding mixture in the cooled shell. Top with the berries. Refrigerate 2 hours or until serving time.
Just before serving, sprinkle with powdered sugar. Store in the refrigerator.

recipes.title: Popcorn Balls
steps: Boil the sugar, Karo, water and vinegar till it spins a thread.
Add the butter. Boil till it forms a hard ball in cold water.
Add the soda and remove from the fire.
Pour over the popcorn and form into balls. Food coloring may be added.
notes: Hard-ball stage is about 250° to 265°F on a candy thermometer.
flags: No amount of popcorn; about 4 to 5 quarts is typical for this much syrup.

recipes.title: Equal Cinnamon Bread Pudding
ingredients: 16 packets Equal sweetener, or 5 teaspoons Equal for Recipes, or 2/3 cup Equal Spoonful
4 cups cubed day-old French or Italian bread (3/4 inch)
steps: Heat the milk and margarine to simmering in a medium saucepan. Remove from heat and stir until the margarine melts. Cool 10 minutes.
Beat the egg and egg whites in a large bowl until foamy. Mix in the Equal, spices and salt. Mix the milk into the egg mixture, then mix in the bread.
Spoon into an ungreased 1 1/2-quart casserole. Place the casserole in a roasting pan on the oven rack and add 1 inch of hot water.
Bake uncovered at 350°F for 40 to 45 minutes, until set and a knife inserted halfway between center and edge comes out clean.
notes: 34% fewer calories than the traditional recipe. 202 calories per serving.

recipes.title: Lemon Cream Freeze
recipes.format: Printed recipe card, front and back
ingredients: 1/2 C graham cracker crumbs (1/4 C for the pan, 1/4 C for the top)
steps: Beat the egg whites, adding the sugar while beating, until stiff and glossy.
Beat the egg yolks until thick and carefully fold into the egg whites.
Whip the cream until soft peaks form. Add the lemon juice and rind and beat until stiff peaks. Fold into the egg mixture.
Sprinkle 1/4 C graham cracker crumbs over the bottom of a greased 8" square pan.
Spoon the egg and cream mixture over the crumbs and top with the other 1/4 C crumbs.
Refrigerate or freeze.
notes: The eggs aren't cooked; pasteurized eggs are the safe choice today.
flags: No amounts for the lemon juice and rind; about 1/3 cup juice and 1 tsp grated rind is typical.

recipes.title: Danish Puffs
ingredients: Frosting: 1 cup powdered sugar, 1/2 teaspoon vanilla, dash of salt, 1 to 2 tablespoons milk
steps: Cut 1/2 cup butter into 1 cup flour until it resembles coarse meal. Stir in the cold water and work the dough until blended.
Shape into a ball and divide in half. Pat each half into a 3x12-inch oblong on a baking sheet.
Bring 1 cup water and the remaining 1/2 cup butter to a boil in a saucepan. Remove from heat and add the almond extract. Quickly stir in the remaining 1 cup flour.
Add the eggs one at a time, beating well with a spoon after each. Spread this thick mixture over the oblongs.
Bake at 400° for about 45 minutes, until puffed and golden.
Meanwhile, blend the powdered sugar, vanilla, salt and enough milk to spread. Frost the pastries while hot. Cut in slices and serve warm.
notes: Also known as Danish puff or almond puff loaf: a pastry base with a cream-puff topping.

recipes.title: Doritos Taco Salad
recipes.format: Handwritten striped card, plus an earlier note on Vision MS notepad paper
ingredients: Dressing of your choice (the note uses Miracle Whip and ketchup)
steps: Brown the ground beef, add the taco seasoning, and set aside.
In a large bowl, add the lettuce, cheese, ground beef and Doritos.
Add whatever dressing you choose to top.
notes: One of Tammy's cards (the striped ones are hers).
The short note on Vision MS paper lists iceberg lettuce, Miracle Whip, ketchup, cheddar and Nacho Doritos, initialed "GB."
flags: Who "GB" on the note is isn't known.

recipes.title: Strawberry Squares
ingredients: Crust: 1 c. flour, 1/4 c. brown sugar, 1/2 c. walnuts, 1/2 c. butter
1 c. white sugar (2/3 c. if frozen berries are used)
2 c. fresh or 10 oz. frozen strawberries
steps: Mix the flour, brown sugar, walnuts and butter and press into a 13x9x2 pan.
Bake 20 minutes at 350°, stirring frequently for even browning. Reserve 1/3 of the crumbs for the top.
Combine the egg whites, sugar, lemon juice and strawberries and beat on high speed 10 minutes.
Fold in whipped cream. Spoon over the crust and sprinkle the rest of the crumbs over the top.
Freeze at least 6 hours before serving.
notes: "Very rich!"
"Stir frequently" means the crust is baked as loose crumbs, then pressed in.
flags: The contributor's name could read Linda or Anda Cummings.
No amount for the whipped cream; about 1 cup whipping cream, whipped, is typical.

recipes.title: 5 Cup Salad
steps: Mix in order in a large bowl.
flags: Drain the pineapple and oranges well first.

recipes.title: Pistachio Green Salad
steps: Mix and fold everything together.
notes: Also known as Watergate salad. Signed "Elinor Best."
flags: The pineapple is usually added with its juice, which sets the pudding.

recipes.title: Southern Ambrosia Salad
ingredients: 1 (20 ounce) can pineapple tidbits, drained well
1 (15 ounce) can mandarin oranges, drained well
1 cup red seedless grapes, sliced in half
1 (10 ounce) jar maraschino cherries, cut in half and drained well
steps: Mix together well.
notes: One of Tammy's cards (the striped ones are hers).

recipes.title: 24-Hour Salad (partial)
steps: Beat the eggs and add the sugar and vinegar.
Cook over very low heat, or in a double boiler, until thick and smooth.
Remove… (the card ends here).
notes: The usual finish: remove from heat, stir in the butter, cool, fold in the whipped cream, fruit and marshmallows, and chill 24 hours.
flags: The directions end mid-sentence. If there's a back to this card, it'd be worth a photo.

recipes.title: Pea Salad
ingredients: Grated sweet pickle or sweet relish
Dressing: Miracle Whip, vinegar and mustard
steps: Combine the peas, cheese, pickle, eggs and onion.
Dress with Miracle Whip thinned with a little vinegar and mustard.
flags: No amounts on the card; mix to taste.

recipes.title: Roquefort Dressing
steps: Mix in order and beat well.
notes: A big batch: nearly 3 quarts. Signed "Margarete Boyington."
flags: The buttermilk amount reads 2/3 qt.

recipes.title: Fruit Salad (Jan Vaniman's)
recipes.format: Printed watermelon recipe card, front and back
steps: Drain the juices from the fruit (the oranges and pineapple chunks).
Add the strawberries and peach pie filling, then blend in the bananas and grapes.
Chill before serving. Will keep several days.
notes: "Vicky Sharp" is written at the top: Vicky's card, with Jan Vaniman's recipe.
From the card: if the salad is made the day before, wait to add the bananas until the day it's served.

recipes.title: Lemonade Fruit Tip
steps: Sprinkle pre-sweetened dry lemonade mix over cut fruit.
notes: "Terrific taste & keeps fruit from turning dark."

recipes.title: Three Bean Salad
steps: Drain the beans thoroughly. Toss with the onion and green pepper.
Blend the remaining ingredients, adding as much sugar as desired. Pour over the vegetables.
Cover and refrigerate several hours or overnight.
At serving time, drain the salad and serve in lettuce cups.
notes: Four Bean Salad: add 1 1-pound can garbanzo beans, drained.

recipes.title: Lemon Cucumbers
steps: Slice the cucumbers and toss with lemon juice, olive oil, salt and pepper.
Sprinkle garlic over the top.
notes: One of Tammy's cards (the striped ones are hers).
flags: No amounts or directions on the card; mix to taste.

recipes.title: Beet Pickles
ingredients: Beets, cooked and sliced or diced
steps: Mix the sugar, water, vinegar, lemon and spices and bring to a boil.
Add the cooked, sliced or diced beets and simmer for 15 minutes.
Put in hot sterilized jars and seal.
notes: Spelled "Picklos" on the card.
flags: The contributor's name could read Lass or Lase.
No amount of beets; this much syrup covers several pounds.
For shelf storage, today's guidance is to process filled jars in a boiling-water bath.

recipes.title: Golden Glow Relish
steps: Grind the cucumbers, onions and peppers and add the salt. Let stand about 12 hours.
Drain, and add the sugars, vinegar and spices.
Cook for 20 minutes and seal in jars.
notes: "From Bernita Jones in Iowa."
flags: For shelf storage, today's guidance is to process filled jars in a boiling-water bath.

recipes.title: Hot Tea Punch
recipes.format: Printed "Here's what's cookin'" card, front and back
ingredients: 1 can, or more, frozen orange juice
steps: Tie the spices loosely in a bag and bring to a boil in the water.
Add the tea (tied loosely in a bag) and steep 5 minutes. Remove the bags.
Add the juices and sugar, bring to a boil, and serve.
notes: May be made ahead and stored in the refrigerator. Reheat when ready to serve.
From Linda Cummings, who also gave the Strawberry Squares (No. 162).

recipes.title: Slow Cooker Pasta Fagioli Soup
recipes.format: Handwritten striped card, front and back
ingredients: 1 (15 oz) can cannellini beans, drained and rinsed
1 (15 oz) can red kidney beans, drained and rinsed
steps: Add the olive oil to a large skillet. Add the ground beef and cook until fully browned.
Place the beef in the slow cooker with the rest of the ingredients except the beans and noodles.
Cook on low 7 to 8 hours or on high 3 to 4 hours.
Put the beans and noodles in a half hour before done.
Remove the bay leaves before serving.
notes: One of Tammy's cards (the striped ones are hers).
Signed off with a heart and "yummy."

recipes.title: Zuppa Toscana Soup
recipes.format: Handwritten striped card, front and back
steps: Fry the sausage, drain, and set aside.
In a large pot, add the onion, potatoes, garlic, broth and water. Bring to a boil, then reduce to medium heat. Cook until the potatoes are done (30 min).
Add the sausage and let boil about 10 minutes.
Add the kale (not the stems) and let simmer 25 minutes.
Bring down to low heat. Add the whipping cream and red pepper flakes and heat through, about another 15 minutes.
notes: One of Tammy's cards (the striped ones are hers).
A copy of the Olive Garden soup.

recipes.title: Noodles
ingredients: 1 1/2 C flour, plus enough to make it very stiff
steps: Mix the eggs and milk.
Add the salt and enough flour to make a very stiff dough.
Roll out, cut in 1/4" strips, and dry at least 2 hours.
Cook in chicken or beef broth.

recipes.title: Spätzle
ingredients: Butter and bread crumbs, to finish
steps: Mix and push through a spätzle machine or colander into boiling water.
Fry in butter and sprinkle with bread crumbs.
Serve with Porcupines.
notes: The Porcupines are No. 096 and No. 105, whose card also says they're "real good with spätzle."

recipes.title: French Fries (Low Calorie)
steps: Set the oven at 475°.
Cut the raw potatoes in strips.
Drop them in a bowl containing the oil and water, mixed. Stir the potatoes until well coated.
Bake for 1/2 hour in the hot oven and serve hot!
notes: Will serve 4 or 5 people.

recipes.title: Special Potato Soup
steps: Cook the potatoes, onions, celery and carrots together, in proportion.
For the potato soup, then add the clams and milk.
Thicken a little.
notes: "Recipe from: Vi Sharp." Really a clam chowder.
flags: No amounts on the card.

recipes.title: Medley Vegetable Soup
recipes.contributor: American Diabetes Association, Special Celebrations and Parties Cookbook (1989)
ingredients: 1 cup fresh or frozen green beans, chopped
2 Tbsp fresh minced tarragon leaves, or 1 Tbsp dried
steps: Combine all ingredients in a saucepan or slow cooker.
Cook until the vegetables are tender.
notes: Exchange: 1 vegetable.

recipes.title: Apple Butter
recipes.format: Handwritten striped card, front and back
ingredients: 6 1/2 lbs apples (Gala), peeled, cored and sliced
steps: Place the apples in the slow cooker. Add the sugars, cinnamon, salt and vanilla and mix well.
Cook on low for about 10 hours, stirring every 2 hours. It should be thick and dark brown.
Use a blender to puree until smooth.
Cover and refrigerate up to 2 weeks, or freeze.
notes: One of Tammy's cards (the striped ones are hers).
flags: The brown sugar line says just "1/2"; cup assumed.

recipes.title: Cabbage Soup (7-Day Diet)
steps: Cut up the ingredients and cover with water.
Bring to a boil and boil 10 minutes.
Simmer about 2 hours, or until the vegetables are tender.
notes: The sheet is the old "cabbage soup diet": this soup plus a day-by-day eating plan for a week. Only the soup is typed up here; the photo shows the rest.
flags: The ingredient list at the top is badly faded; it's read from what's visible plus the usual version of this recipe.

recipes.title: Texas Roadhouse Honey Butter
steps: Mix well.
notes: One of Tammy's cards (the striped ones are hers).

recipes.title: Chex Mix
recipes.format: Handwritten striped card, front and back
steps: Preheat oven to 250°.
In a large aluminum tin, mix the cereal, nuts and pretzels.
Add the liquids and seasonings to the melted butter and stir together.
Pour over the cereal, nuts and pretzels until covered.
Bake, stirring every ten minutes, for 50 minutes.
notes: One of Tammy's cards (the striped ones are hers).

recipes.title: Sugary Sweet Chex Mix
recipes.format: Handwritten striped card, front and back
steps: Put the Chex into a large bowl.
In a medium saucepan, put the syrup, sugar and butter. Heat over medium to high heat, stirring regularly, until dissolved and boiling.
When boiling, stir constantly for 3 minutes. Remove from heat carefully.
Pour the mixture over the cereal and stir with a rubber spatula until the cereal is covered.
To keep it chewy, spread the mixture out on 2 or 3 cookie sheets. Spray your hands with cooking spray so the cereal won't stick while separating.
Stir every 15 minutes until cooled. Store in a dry space.
notes: One of Tammy's cards (the striped ones are hers).
The savory version is No. 186.

recipes.title: Chip Clam Dip
steps: Blend everything together until smooth enough to dip chips.
notes: Just an ingredient list, with "Chip Clam Dip" written at the bottom.
flags: No amounts or directions.
Something below "onion" is scribbled out.

recipes.title: Salmon Party Ball
recipes.format: Printed "Here's what's cookin'" card, front and back, plus the original clipping
steps: Drain and flake the salmon, removing skin and bones.
Combine the salmon, cream cheese, lemon juice, onion, horseradish, salt and liquid smoke. Mix thoroughly. Chill several hours.
Combine the pecans and parsley. Shape the salmon mixture into a ball and roll in the nut mixture.
Chill well. Serve with assorted crackers.
notes: "Recipe from: Brenda Sharp." The newspaper clipping it came from is in the box too.

recipes.title: Cheese Ball (Vi Sharp's)
recipes.format: Two cards: "Here's what's cookin'" card and printed recipe card

photos.label: Second copy, from a Tupperware demonstrator

ingredients: 1/2 glass Old English, cheddar or pineapple cheese spread
Chopped pecans and parsley flakes, for rolling
steps: Add the onion salt and garlic salt to the cheeses and A-1 and mix well with a fork.
Roll into two baseball-size balls.
Roll in chopped pecans and parsley flakes.
Refrigerate. Can be frozen.
notes: "Recipe from the kitchen of: Vi Sharp." Makes about 2 baseball-size balls.
A second copy says it came from a Tupperware demonstrator.
Different from the Cheese Ball (No. 001) from Edi Dobbins.

recipes.title: Tortilla Chip Dip (7 Layer Dip)
steps: Layer in a dish or pan.
Serve with tortilla chips.
flags: The contributor's name reads Erica Brooks.
No amounts on the card.

recipes.title: Sliced Baked Potatoes
recipes.format: Handwritten striped card, front and back
steps: Heat oven to 400°. Slice the potatoes 1/4 inch thick and place on a foiled cookie sheet.
Brush both sides with melted butter. Bake 30 to 40 minutes, turning once.
Remove from the oven. Cover with cheddar cheese, bacon and green onion.
Place back in the oven until the cheese is melted.
Remove from oven. Add sour cream if desired.
notes: One of Tammy's cards (the striped ones are hers).
flags: The back (a green card) turned up separately; matched by the handwriting and the last step.

recipes.title: Zucchini Casserole
ingredients: 1/4 cup grated Parmesan or Romano cheese
steps: Sauté the zucchini, onion, garlic, oregano and basil in the oil until the zucchini is tender.
Spoon into a lightly oiled casserole dish.
Combine the remaining ingredients and pour over the zucchini.
Bake at 350° for 15 to 20 minutes, or until browned. Let stand 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Exchanges: 1 vegetable, 2 fats. Same typed style as the Medley Vegetable Soup (No. 182).

recipes.title: Cheesy Baked Macaroni
ingredients: 1/2 lb. Kraft Deluxe Pasteurized Process American Cheese, cubed
1 cup (3 1/2 oz.) elbow macaroni, cooked and drained
steps: Heat oven to 350°F.
Stir the cheese and milk in a saucepan on low heat until smooth.
Stir in the macaroni and pepper. Spoon into a 1-quart casserole.
Bake 20 minutes.

recipes.title: Drop Doughnuts
ingredients: 1/2 C milk, plus a little more
steps: Mix the flour, sugar, salt, baking powder and cinnamon.
Combine the egg, milk and shortening.
Add the wet to the dry and mix.
Drop by teaspoons into hot grease, about 360°, until golden brown.
notes: "1/4 t cinnamon" is written in darker ink over the original spice line, which may have been nutmeg.
flags: The salt amount is under a stain; about 1/2 tsp is typical.
The card is faded; the amounts are best readings.

recipes.title: Chex Party Mix (1981 Original)
recipes.format: Cut from a cereal box (Ralston Purina, 1981)
ingredients: 1 cup salted mixed nuts and/or pretzel sticks
steps: Preheat oven to 250°.
Heat the margarine in a large shallow roasting pan (about 15 x 10 x 2 inch) in the oven until melted. Remove.
Stir in the seasoned salt and Worcestershire sauce. Add the Chex cereal and nuts, and mix until all pieces are coated.
Heat in the oven 1 hour, stirring every 15 minutes.
Spread on absorbent paper to cool.
notes: "Is this the Christmas you finally make enough Chex Party Mix?" From a 1981 Chex box.
Chex Party Mix may be frozen, so make a double batch. Thaw at room temperature in the container it was stored in.
Tammy's version is No. 186.

recipes.title: Egg Color Solution
steps: Mix the vinegar and food color first, then add the water.
Use as many food coloring drops as needed.
notes: For dyeing Easter eggs.

recipes.title: Play Dough
ingredients: 2 teaspoons cream of tartar (do not omit)
steps: Combine and mix all the dry ingredients.
Add the water slowly, then the oil and food coloring.
Cook for 3 minutes, or until the mixture forms a ball.
Knead as soon as possible.
Keep in an airtight container.
notes: Homemade play dough for kids. Not for eating.

recipes.title: Coal Plant (Crystal Garden)
ingredients: 2 or 3 lumps of coal or charcoal
steps: Place the coal or charcoal in a small dish or pan. Sprinkle with 3 tablespoons salt, 3 tablespoons water and 1 tablespoon bluing.
Next morning, add 3 tablespoons salt and 3 tablespoons water.
The third morning, add 3 more tablespoons salt, 3 tablespoons water and 1 drop of Mercurochrome.
The "plant" should begin to grow in about 1 week. As the moisture evaporates, add more sprinkles of water.
notes: An old-fashioned crystal garden, not food. The crystals grow up out of the coal.
Mercurochrome contained mercury and isn't sold in the US anymore; a drop of food coloring gives the color instead. Keep bluing away from kids and pets.
